07-017.r: Most powerful state of the early 6th century B.C. → Magadha, the richest Mahajanapada; rivals: Koshala, Anga, Kashi.

07-018.r: Not an early (Buddha-period) republic → Yaudheya. Republics then: Shakya (Kapilavastu), Lichchhavi (Vaishali), Malla (Kusinara, Pava), Koliya, Moriya, Videha.

07-019.r: World's first republic (6th century B.C.) → Lichchhavis of Vaishali; Vaishali named after King Vishal; birthplace of Mahavira.

07-021.r: Correct pair → Chetak–Lichchhavi (chief of the Lichchhavi republic, a clan of the Vajji union); his daughter Chelana married Bimbisara.

07-022.r: List of 16 Mahajanapadas → Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist) and Bhagavati Sutra (Jain); from Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Koshala to Gandhara, Kamboj.

07-025.r: Panini (born Pushkalavati, Gandhara) → Ashtadhyayi (about 4000 sutras) names 22 Janapadas, three most important: Magadha, Ashmak, Kamboj.

07-027.r: Panchala capitals: North → Ahichchhatra; South → Kampilya. Kuru → Hastinapur, Indraprastha; Shurasena → Mathura.
07-027.t: Ahichchhatra = North Panchala; Kampilya = South Panchala.

07-029.r: Champa → capital of Anga (Munger, Bhagalpur, Bihar); Anga annexed to Magadha by Bimbisara.

07-030.r: Suktimati (Sotthivati) → capital of Chedi Mahajanapada (Bundelkhand), sixth century B.C.

07-031.r: Mahajanapada on the Godavari → Assaka (Ashmaka), between Godavari and Narmada; capital Paithan/Potan (Pratishthana).

07-032.r: Matsya Mahajanapada (6th century B.C.) → Rajasthan (Jaipur, Alwar, Bharatpur); capital Viratnagar.

07-033.r: First capital of Magadha → Girivraja (Rajgriha/Rajgir), made capital by Jarasandha (Brihadrath dynasty); Udayin later moved it to Pataliputra.

07-035.r: First capital of Magadha → Rajgriha (Girivraj), not among options → 'none of the above'; Udayin (Haryanka) moved it to Pataliputra.

07-037.r: Not a Magadhan capital → Kaushambi (capital of Vatsa). Magadha's capitals: Girivraja/Rajgriha, then Pataliputra (shifted by Udayin).

07-038.r: Ancient Shravasti (Sahet-Mahet, identified by Cunningham in 1861) → crescent-shaped town plan.

07-039.r: Ajatashatru (492-460 BC) → killed his father Bimbisara (Haryanka founder) for the throne; was killed by his son Udayin for the same reason.
07-039.t: Udayin of Magadha is not Udayan of Vatsa.

07-043.r: Vajjis (Lichchhavi capital Vaishali) defeated and merged into Magadha → Ajatashatru; Lichchhavi chief Chetak had formed a united front against him.

07-044.r: Magadha's power extended over Malwa (Avanti) → Shishunaga, who defeated Nandivardhan (Matsya Purana).

07-045.r: Founder of the Nanda dynasty (after the Shishunagas) → Mahapadmananda (Ugrasen); Puranas call him Sarvakshatrantaka and Aparoparashurama.

07-048.r: Varanasi (Kashi's capital) → came to Bimbisara as dowry; Ajatashatru gained suzerainty over Kashi; Shishunag, ruling from Vaishali, made his son deputy-king at Varanasi.
07-048.c: No answer printed; the shown explanation leans to Shishunag but does not state who made Varanasi the second capital.

07-049.r: After the Nanda dynasty (first Ugrasen/Mahapadmananda, last Dhanananda; heavy taxes made people restless) → Maurya dynasty ruled Magadha.

07-050.r: Inscriptional evidence of King Nanda → Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription (Chedi dynasty of Kalinga): Mahapadmananda's canal in Kalinga; first inscription mentioning canals.

07-051.r: Magadhan dynasties in order → Haryanka (544-412 BC) → Nanda (344-321 BC) → Maurya (321-185 BC) → Shunga (185-75 BC).

07-052.r: Jivaka, famous physician of Buddha's time → court of Bimbisara; Bimbisara sent him to treat Avanti king Chanda Pradyota.

07-054.r: Sixth century B.C. → great religious upheaval (many new sects in the middle Ganga valley and elsewhere); Vedic religion had become complex → both true.

07-055.r: Kalpi (Jalaun, U.P.) → on the Yamuna; ancient Kalpriya Nagari, built by King Vasudeva in the 4th century A.D.

07-056.r: Kuru → Indraprastha; Panchal → Ahichchhatra; Kosala → Saket; Vatsa → Kaushambi.

07-057.r: Matsya → Viratnagar; Kuru → Indraprastha; Shurasena → Mathura; Asmak → Potan.

07-058.r: Correct: Asmaka → Godavari; Kosala → Sarayu. Wrong: Kamboja → Kubha (Kabul), not Vipas; Avanti → Shipra, Narmada, not Mahanadi → only two.

07-059.r: Wrong pair: Shurasena belongs to Mathura (Yadava rulers), not Kaushambi. Correct: Kamboj-Rajpur/Hatak, Ashmak-Potan/Potil, Koshal-Shravasti.

07-060.r: Mahajanapadas in present U.P. → 8 of 16: Kuru, Panchala, Shurasena, Vatsa, Koshal, Malla, Kashi, Chedi.

07-061.r: Not true: 'Shreni system only in North India' – it existed in North and South. Shreni = guild of traders and artisans fixing quality, price, members' conduct.

08-001.r: Dynasty in North India at Alexander's invasion → Nanda; contemporary king Dhanananda (Greek 'Agrammese'), commander Bhaddasala.

08-003.r: Alexander left India in 325 B.C. after about two years' campaign (true); he was not defeated by Chandragupta Maurya (false) → A true, R false.

08-004.r: Women who took up arms against Alexander → Massaga, capital of the Ashvaka republic.

08-005.r: Alexander's success → no central power in India (28 independent powers), superior army, help of traitor rulers like Ambhi; not his administration → 1, 2, 3.

08-006.r: Indian king defeated by Alexander on the Jhelum → Porus (Puru), ruler between Jhelum and Chenab; impressed, Alexander returned his kingdom.

08-007.r: Did not come with Alexander → Deimachus, envoy of Seleucid king Antiochus to Bindusara's court (Strabo). Came with him: Nearchus, Onesicritus, Aristobulus.

09-001.r: First Indian empire → Chandragupta Maurya; first to unify India politically, empire up to the edge of present Iran.

09-003.r: Oldest dynasty among options → Maurya (321-185 B.C.), founded by Chandragupta Maurya; later Kushan, Gupta (275-550 CE), Vardhana.

09-005.r: Chandragupta Maurya features in → Vishakhadatta's 'Mudrarakshasa' (calls him 'Vrishal', 'Kulheen'); commentary by Dhundiraja.
